# The volume seed controls every terminal min-plus price through depth twelve

**Date:** 2026-08-07  
**Status:** unconditional all-price theorem for the terminal even
parent/child pairs at depths nine, ten, eleven, and twelve.  The proof uses
the exact binomial birth formula, the residue-prefix lemma, and eight
explicit cyclic Apéry routes.  It does not claim an all-depth theorem.

## 1. Common coefficient measure

For \(n=2r\), put

\[
 H_s^{(n)}={n\choose s}-{n\choose s-1},
 \qquad
 \widetilde H_1^{(n)}=n,
 \qquad
 \widetilde H_s^{(n)}=H_s^{(n)}\quad(s\ne1),
\tag{1.1}
\]

and

\[
 V_{r,D}
 =D{2r\choose r}-\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}{2r\choose j}.
\tag{1.2}
\]

With \(t=r-D\), define

\[
 \nu_{r,D}(L)=
 {\bf1}_{1\le L\le D}H_{t+L}^{(2r)}
 -\widetilde H_{t-L}^{(2r)}
 \qquad(1\le L\le t-1),
\tag{1.3}
\]

and set it to zero otherwise.  For a terminal parent \(r\) and its child
\(r-1\), the integer-scaled volume-normalized coefficient is

\[
\boxed{
 \widehat\mu_L
 =V_{r-1,D}\nu_{r,D}(L)
  -V_{r,D}\nu_{r-1,D}(L).}
\tag{1.4}
\]

The birth-volume identity gives

\[
 \sum_LL\nu_{r,D}(L)=V_{r,D},
 \qquad
 \sum_LL\widehat\mu_L=0.
\tag{1.5}
\]

Consequently

\[
 V_{r-1,D}\left(
 M_{2r,D}(\psi)
 -{V_{r,D}\over V_{r-1,D}}M_{2r-2,D}(\psi)
 \right)
 =\sum_L\widehat\mu_L\psi(L).
\tag{1.6}
\]

All arithmetic certificates below are direct integer substitutions in
(1.1)--(1.4).  The routes were not selected by a numerical optimizer.

Every coefficient after \(D\) is negative by a symbolic ratio argument,
not by a sign scan.  For \(D+1\le L\le t-3\), put \(s=t-L\).  The exact
identity

\[
 {H_s^{(2r)}\over H_{s-1}^{(2r-2)}}
 ={(2r)(2r-1)\over s(2r+1-s)}
\tag{2.6}
\]

is minimized at \(s=r-2D-1\) on the relevant range.  The four lower
bounds are

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
D&s_{\max}&
\displaystyle\min_s{H_s^{(2r)}\over H_{s-1}^{(2r-2)}}\\ \hline
9&95&1362/335>4\\
10&119&620/153>4\\
11&145&469/116>4\\
12&173&39105/9688>4
\end{array}
\tag{2.7}
\]

while (2.3) gives \(V_{r,D}/V_{r-1,D}<2\).  Hence the tail coefficient
in (1.4) is negative.  At \(L=t-2\),

\[
 -V_{r-1,D}H_2^{(2r)}+V_{r,D}(2r-2)<0
\tag{2.8}
\]

because \(H_2^{(2r)}>2(2r-2)\) and the volume ratio is below two.
At \(L=t-1\), only the negative parent rank-one birth remains.
Therefore

\[
\boxed{
 \widehat\mu_1,\ldots,\widehat\mu_{D-1}>0,
 \qquad
 \widehat\mu_L<0\quad(D\le L\le t-1).}
\tag{2.9}
\]

## 3. All noncritical residue systems pass by prefixes

For \(2\le h\le D\) and \(1\le a<h\), put

\[
 S_{h,a}=\sum_{j\ge0}\widehat\mu_{a+jh}.
\tag{3.1}
\]

The following four entries are minima over **every** displayed
denomination and every nonzero residue:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|r}
D&2\le h\le h_0&\operatorname*{argmin}(h,a)&
\displaystyle\min_{2\le h\le h_0,\ 1\le a<h}S_{h,a}\\ \hline

\end{array}
\tag{3.2}
\]

By (2.9), each residue sequence starts with positive coefficients and
then contains only negative coefficients.  It therefore rises and then
decreases to its positive total in (3.2).  Every prefix is nonnegative.
The residue-prefix lemma proves the desired all-price inequality for

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
D&\text{minimum-density denominations already closed}\\ \hline
9&h\le7\\
10&h\le8\\
11&h\le9\\
12&h\le10.
\end{array}
\tag{3.3}
\]

The case \(h=1\) is the tight linear price.

Every number in the last column is strictly positive.  Hence all shared
piece capacities remain nonnegative.  The partition identities show
that every route belongs to the corresponding set

\[
 \mathcal X_a=
 \left\{x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{h-1}:
 \sum_{i=1}^{h-1}ix_i=h+a,\ 
 x_i=0\text{ on deficit residues}\right\}.
\tag{4.3}
\]

Thus (4.2) is a literal feasible solution of the compressed cyclic Apéry
transport LP.  The depth-eight transport theorem applies and proves all
eight remaining minimum-density cases.

For clarity, the two multidefect capacity comparisons in (4.2) are
exactly

\[
\begin{aligned}
D=12,\ h=11:\quad&
S_5\ge\Delta_1,\quad
S_6\ge\Delta_2,\quad
S_7\ge\Delta_1+\Delta_2,\\
D=12,\ h=12:\quad&
S_6\ge\Delta_1+\Delta_{11},\quad
S_7\ge\Delta_1,\quad
S_8\ge\Delta_{11},\quad
S_9\ge\Delta_{11}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.4}
\]

These are shared-capacity inequalities, not independent
single-deficit checks.

## 5. Exact theorem

### Theorem 5.1

For each

\[
 D\in\{9,10,11,12\},
\qquad
 r\in\{114,140,168,198\}
\tag{5.1}
\]

in the corresponding order, every closed depth-\(D\) piece table and its
complete min-plus closure satisfy

\[
\boxed{
 M_{2r,D}(\psi)
 -{V_{r,D}\over V_{r-1,D}}M_{2r-2,D}(\psi)\ge0.}
\tag{5.2}
\]

Equivalently, the exact minimum central weight for a unit
distance-one pair is

\[
\boxed{
 \rho_D^{\rm vol}
 =2-{V_{r,D}\over V_{r-1,D}}.}
\tag{5.3}
\]

The linear price is tight by (1.5), so no smaller central weight can
work.  Every depth-\(D\) min-plus fan ray is nonnegative at this weight,
and Pascal convolution therefore propagates each seed as a nonnegative
weighted invariant orbit.

## 6. Scope

This extends the exact all-price frontier from depth eight through depth
twelve.  It does not show that the displayed sparse routes persist at
arbitrary depth.  Depth twelve is already genuinely multidefect at both
of its last denominations, and the two routes share residue seven at
\(h=11\) and residue six at \(h=12\).  The general remaining theorem is
still feasibility of the binomial cyclic transport LP, or an equivalent
uniform Farkas cut.
